Our sentence transplants the shoyu onto the tare and drops the salt entirely. The gluten conclusion is unchanged and in fact stronger than we wrote it: the noodles are 「麺屋

vegan_cross_contact.text: The dipping broth is a pork-bone and chicken-collagen base finished with Iberico pork belly, and the bowl is topped with pork belly and sous-vide pork chashu — animal-based throughout.

cultural_comfort.note: A polished, design-forward lunch-only tsukemen counter intended to feel welcoming even to solo diners; a friendly greeting and pointing at the signature bowl will carry you, though staff likely operate mainly in Japanese.

kyr_akete_mo_kurete_mo.gf_detail: This is Jiro-style ramen: thick wheat noodles in a pork-bone broth (or as a brothless 汁なし bowl) built on a soy-based tare. Wheat is present in both the noodles and the soy seasoning, and there is no indication of any gluten-free option or accommodation. Not suitable for celiacs or anyone strictly avoiding gluten.
kyr_akete_mo_kurete_mo.vegan_detail: A pork-centric Jiro-style shop: pork-bone broth, large slabs of chashu, and pork back-fat are core to every bowl, with mountains of bean sprouts and raw garlic as standard toppings. There is no vegan or vegetarian bowl, and no indication that one can be made.
kyr_akete_mo_kurete_mo.notes: [Mom & Pop] The shop sits in the lineage of "Yume Wo Katare Kyoto," the dream-fueled Jiro-style ramen project that opened in this Senbon-Nakatachiuri neighborhood in 2017. True to the Yume Wo Katare ethos, where a location either closes or is reborn under a new name after a set run, the seco

chef_bio.background: The shop sits in the lineage of "Yume Wo Katare Kyoto," the dream-fueled Jiro-style ramen project whose second location in this Senbon-Nakatachiuri neighborhood (Yume Wo Katare Kyoto II) opened on November 29, 2017. True to the Yume Wo Katare ethos, where a location is restructured or reborn under a new name after a set run, the shop was rebranded on April 1, 2025 as あけてもくれても after owner Teru took the whole place over, carrying the same hulking bowls into a new identity.
chef_bio.philosophy: Carry forward the Yume Wo Katare spirit of generous, soul-filling ramen and the discipline of reinventing the shop rather than letting it stagnate, while keeping the experience honest, hands-on, and built around the counter.
chef_bio.specialty: A classic Jiro-style (Ramen Sou-lineage) bowl: ultra-thick, chewy wheat noodles in a sweet soy-and-pork-bone broth, crowned with a fat slab of chashu, a mountain of bean sprouts, back-fat, and garlic. The house also leans into a signature 汁なし (brothless) version, a nod echoed in the playful name.

anecdotes.text: The shop's name, あけてもくれても ("whether it opens or closes / day in, day out"), winks at both its rebirth from Yume Wo Katare and its embrace of the brothless 汁なし bowl.
It traces directly back to Yume Wo Katare Kyoto II, opened November 2017, whose tradition of renaming or restarting a shop after its run led to this April 2025 incarnation under Teru.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: osumituki.com confirms the shop name changed from 'Yume Wo Katare Kyoto II' (opened 2017-11-29) to 'あけても くれても' on 2025-04-01, Jiro/二郎系 style with sweet pork broth and 汁なし options, in Kamigyo-ku's Senbon-Nakatachiuri. noodlers.jp confirms current owner てる (Teru) took over the whole shop under the Yume Wo Katare 'restructure after a run' philosophy, that it specializes in 汁なし, and the name's play on words.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The bowls are built on a sweet soy-based tare over wheat noodles, so wheat is present in both the seasoning and the noodles.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Pork-bone broth, large chashu, and pork back-fat are standard across the menu, with no meat-free preparation noted.

cultural_comfort.note: A no-frills, locals-and-students Jiro-style counter where you order outside, wait to be called in, and call your toppings ("ニンニク・アブラ・ヤサイ") in Japanese at the counter, so first-timers without a guide or some prep can find the ritual intimidating.

kyr_gokuboso_seiryu_ramen.gf_detail: No gluten-free provision. This is a Jiro-inspired ramen shop built around extremely thick wheat noodles, served with a sweet wheat-shoyu-based tare and a pork broth — the entire concept is wheat-noodle-centric. There is no indication of GF noodles, GF tare, allergen handling, or a dedicated preparation area. A celiac diner cannot eat safely here.
kyr_gokuboso_seiryu_ramen.vegan_detail: Not vegan-friendly. The bowls are built on pork (chashu/meat toppings) and an animal-based broth with a soy/wheat tare; signature orders are explicitly "with meat" (肉あり). No vegan ramen option is mentioned anywhere in the sources.
kyr_gokuboso_seiryu_ramen.hours_raw: Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri 11:00-14:00 & 18:00-22:00; Sat/Sun 10:30-14:00; closed Wednesdays (and holidays). Note: the owner sometimes closes on short notice when he judges the noodle quality is not up to standard.
kyr_gokuboso_seiryu_ramen.notes: [Mom & Pop] The owner cut his teeth at Nagoya's famed Jiro-inspired shop「ら けいこ」before bringing that gut-punching, big-portion style to a small storefront in southwest Kyoto, a short walk north of Nishi-Oji Station.

chef_bio.origin: Nagoya, via the Jiro-inspired ramen shop「ら・けいこ」(Rakeiko)
chef_bio.background: The owner cut his teeth at Nagoya's Jiro-inspired shop「極太濁流ラーメン ら・けいこ」before bringing that gut-punching, big-portion style to a small storefront in southwest Kyoto's Shimogyo ward, a short walk north of Nishi-Oji Station.
chef_bio.philosophy: Noodles first, no compromise: the owner will close the shop on the spot if he judges the day's noodles aren't good enough — announcing closures on social media, a quality-over-convenience stance that keeps the schedule a little unpredictable but the bowls honest.
chef_bio.specialty: Extra-thick (極太), chewy straight noodles in generous, hearty bowls — a sweet soy-based tare clinging to the noodles, piled with vegetables, meat and garlic. The shop runs both broth (汁あり) and no-broth (汁なし) versions, with a standout no-broth bowl named シルナシノ神 ('the god of soupless'), served with fat-coated noodles, thick tonkatsu-style pork loin, greens, crushed nuts, a fried egg, crisp bean sprouts and minced garlic.

anecdotes.text: Regulars know the shop as a 'those-in-the-know know it' hidden gem, and that the owner has been known to post that he is closing because the noodles didn't come out right that day — quality over keeping the doors open.
The defining feature is the gut-punch (ガツン系) extra-thick noodle, a direct inheritance of the Nagoya「ら・けいこ」lineage the owner trained in.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: guts-rentacar.com (Nishioji) confirms the owner trained at a Nagoya ramen shop, the addictive chewy extra-thick Jiro-inspired noodles, sweet soy broth, ~3-min walk north of Nishioji Station, and the owner closing when noodle quality drops (announced via SNS). Web search of Tabelog/Retty/nagoya-meshi confirms the Nagoya training shop is「極太濁流ラーメン ら・けいこ」and that the signature no-broth bowl is シルナシノ神 (~750 yen).

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Bowls are dressed with a sweet soy-based (shoyu) tare, which in this style is wheat-containing; combined with the wheat noodles there is no celiac-safe path here.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bowls are built on pork and meat toppings with an animal-based broth; no vegan preparation is mentioned.

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny 10-seat counter shop with ticket-machine ordering and no listed phone or English support — comfortable for a visitor with some Japanese or willingness to point and gesture, but plan to order by machine and dine quickly.

kyr_mansei.gf_detail: No gluten-free provision. The chuka-soba is wheat Chinese noodles in a chicken-bone soy (shoyu) broth, and the menu centers on wheat-based udon, soba, ramen, yakisoba, curry and fried tempura items. Soy-based tare and seasonings are standard Japanese shoyu (wheat-containing). There is no indication of allergen handling or a dedicated fryer, so this is not safe for celiac diners.
kyr_mansei.vegan_detail: Not a vegan-friendly shop. The signature chuka-soba uses a chicken-bone (tori-gara) soy broth with roasted pork and kamaboko (fish cake) toppings, and dishes broadly rely on dashi, egg, meat and seafood. No vegan options are advertised.
kyr_mansei.notes: [Mom & Pop] Mansei is a much-loved old-style neighborhood shokudo (taishoku-do / machi-chuka) in the Nishinokyo–Enmachi area of Kyoto, near Enmachi Station and Hanazono University. It is the kind of culturally-valuable corner eatery (described locally as a 文化財的な街の食堂, a culturally-treasured t

chef_bio.background: Mansei is a much-loved old-style neighborhood shokudo (taishoku-do / machi-chuka) in the Nishinokyo–Enmachi area of Kyoto's Nakagyo ward, near Enmachi Station and Hanazono University. It is the kind of culturally-valuable corner eatery (described locally as a 文化財的な街の食堂, a culturally-treasured town diner) that has fed the surrounding neighborhood for generations, with neatly kept food-sample cases in the window, an aged wall menu, manga to read while you wait, and a relaxed table-seat layout. Delivery to local homes and workplaces is part of its everyday rhythm.
chef_bio.philosophy: Honest, affordable, comforting everyday food for the neighborhood — the appeal is the nostalgic, unpretentious shokudo experience rather than any single trend.
chef_bio.specialty: The signature bowl is the chuka-soba: a simple, body-warming chicken-bone soy (tori-gara shoyu) broth topped with kamaboko fish cake, roast pork, bean sprouts and chopped green onion, served with firm, low-hydration Chinese-style noodles. Beyond the chuka-soba the kitchen turns out a wide home-style range — udon, soba, yakisoba, rice bowls, curry, omurice and stir-fries — at gentle prices, with the tenjoji-don (天とじ丼, egg-bound shrimp-tempura rice bowl, around 680 yen) a noted favorite.

anecdotes.text: Reviewers describe the chuka-soba as a simple, comforting chicken-bone soy broth that seems to soak into your body (シンプルで、身体に染み入る鶏ガラ醤油の中華そば), with kamaboko, roast pork, bean sprouts and green onion over firm, low-hydration noodles.
The shop is praised as a culturally-valuable town diner with carefully kept food samples, a well-aged wall menu and manga to browse, with table seating that encourages a leisurely meal.
The tenjoji-don (天とじ丼) is highlighted: two shrimp tempura and rice enveloped in plenty of dashi-infused egg (海老天ぷら2尾とごはんを出汁を含んだたっぷりの玉子が包み込む), around 680 yen.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotopi.jp calls Mansei a 文化財的な街の食堂 ('a place we hope stays forever'), with vintage food samples, an aged wall menu, manga/TV, table-only seating, home & workplace delivery, and the 680-yen 天とじ丼 (two shrimp tempura bound in egg over rice); address 京都市中京区西ノ京北壺井町62, near Enmachi/Hanazono University. v-trip.net confirms the chuka-soba's chicken-bone soy broth, kamaboko/roast pork/sprouts/green onion toppings and firm low-hydration noodles, plus a broad shokudo menu.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Shared kitchen turning out wheat noodles (udon, soba, ramen, yakisoba), tempura and curry; no gluten-free handling indicated, so high cross-contamination risk for celiac diners.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The chuka-soba is a chicken-bone soy (shoyu) broth; standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat and no gluten-free tare is offered.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Broths and dishes rely on chicken-bone stock, dashi, pork, fish cake and egg; no vegan preparation indicated.

cultural_comfort.note: A long-standing local neighborhood diner with handwritten/wall menus in Japanese and no English signage indicated, so a little Japanese or pointing at the food samples will smooth the visit.

kyr_men_star_mu_lucky.gf_detail: This is a wheat-noodle ramen shop. The bowls use standard wheat ramen noodles (from a Kyoto noodle maker) plus a soy-sauce-based tare in the shoyu bowls, and the chicken broths are not gluten-free. No gluten-free menu, noodle substitution, or celiac accommodation is indicated. Not suitable for celiacs or strict gluten avoidance.
kyr_men_star_mu_lucky.vegan_detail: Every signature bowl is built on chicken broth (tori-shoyu, tori-shio, tori-paitan) and topped with pork chashu; the mazesoba and side sets (fried rice, karaage, gyudon) are also meat-based. No vegan or vegetarian option is indicated.
kyr_men_star_mu_lucky.hours_raw: Listed lunch hours 11:30-14:30 (some sources note an earlier 11:00 open and an evening service ~18:00-20:00/21:00); closed Sundays. Hours have varied between sources, so evening availability is uncertain.
kyr_men_star_mu_lucky.notes: [Mom & Pop] A chicken-broth ramen specialist that opened in July 2023 in the Jujo-Omiya neighborhood of Kyoto's Minami ward, just north of a local yakitori shop and a short walk from Kintetsu Jujo Station. It is described as having been opened by someone who trained at a popular Kyoto ramen

chef_bio.background: A chicken-broth ramen specialist that opened on July 17, 2023 in the Jujo-Omiya neighborhood of Kyoto's Minami ward (Nishi-Kujo Morimoto-cho), just north of a local yakitori shop and a short walk from Kintetsu Jujo Station. It is described as having been opened by someone who trained at a popular Kyoto chicken-paitan ramen shop near Nishi-Oji.
chef_bio.philosophy: A focus on the clean umami of chicken - both a light chicken clear broth and a richer chicken paitan - served in a bright, clean, casual room with springy medium-thin straight noodles from the respected Kyoto noodle maker 麺屋棣鄂 (Menya Teigaku).
chef_bio.specialty: Chicken-forward ramen in three styles - tori-shoyu (chicken-soy), tori-shio (chicken-salt) and the signature tori-paitan (creamy chicken broth), plus a mazesoba. The tori-paitan is the recommended bowl, with extra hand-cut scallions a popular add-on; the tori-shoyu pairs a sweet soy tare with chicken-and-bonito dashi.

anecdotes.text: Opened July 17, 2023 by someone said to come from a popular Kyoto ramen shop, with chicken clear broth and chicken paitan as the signature menu.

The tori-paitan is recommended with negi-mashi (extra scallions, +50 yen); the fresh hand-cut scallions are praised for their sweetness and pleasant bite, over a gentle broth with four slices of chashu and sprouts.

The tori-shoyu uses a sweeter soy tare that pairs well with a light chicken clear broth and bonito dashi, finished with bonito flakes and benina radish sprouts; the half fried-rice set is praised for its fluffy, made-to-order wok-fry.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyo-soku.com and osumituki.com date the opening to 2023-07-17 in Minami-ku's Nishi-Kujo Morimoto-cho, with とり醤油 and とり白湯 as signatures; web search (Tabelog/kyotopi) corroborates the owner previously worked at a popular Nishi-Oji chicken-paitan shop. kyotopi.jp confirms four noodle items (tori-paitan, tori-shio, tori-shoyu, mazesoba), +50-yen hand-cut negi-mashi, four chashu slices, and noodles by テイガク (麺屋棣鄂); noodlers.jp confirms the same 麺屋棣鄂 noodles, the tori-shoyu build (soy tare, chicken clear broth + bonito, benina sprouts) and the made-to-order half fried-rice set.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The tori-shoyu bowl is built on a sweet soy-sauce tare, which in Japanese ramen is virtually always wheat-based soy sauce.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, casual neighborhood ramen counter with no indication of English support, so a few Japanese phrases and pointing at the menu will go a long way.

kyr_kyoto_kinkakuji_ramen_na.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. The bowls center on wheat ramen noodles (thin straight noodles), and the broths are paired with a soy-sauce (shoyu) tare and salt versions — shoyu is wheat-based unless stated otherwise, and no gluten-free noodle or tare option is mentioned anywhere. No dedicated handling for celiac diners. A celiac traveler cannot safely eat here.
kyr_kyoto_kinkakuji_ramen_na.vegan_detail: Not suitable for vegans. The entire menu is built on animal stock — a chicken/pork/clam/fish "quadruple" paitan broth — and bowls are topped with multiple kinds of chashu pork and egg. No vegetable-based or vegan broth is offered.
kyr_kyoto_kinkakuji_ramen_na.notes: [Mom & Pop] Nakasawa spent about 18 years cooking ramen across Toyama and Tokyo before coming home to open his own shop near Kinkaku-ji in October 2023. By his own account he never set out to be a chef in the abstract — as he puts it, for him there was only ever ramen.

chef_bio.origin: Born in Kyoto; his family moved to Toyama when he was in middle school.
chef_bio.background: Nakasawa spent about 18 years cooking ramen across Toyama and Tokyo before coming home to open his own shop near Kinkaku-ji in October 2023. By his own account he never set out to be a chef in the abstract — as he puts it, for him there was only ever ramen.
chef_bio.philosophy: He originally planned a clear-broth (chintan) ramen, but mindful of the nearby Ritsumeikan University crowd he reworked it into a creamy-yet-not-overpowering paitan aimed at winning over younger diners. The care shows in details like charcoal-grilled chashu whose smoky aroma carries into the soup — he has been known to ask guests whether they can taste the char.
chef_bio.specialty: The signature is a chicken-paitan bowl built on a so-called 'quadruple' soup: Kyoto Akaji-dori chicken bones, pork bones, Shinji-ko shijimi clams and a seafood blend (niboshi, scallop, bonito and mackerel), finished with a three-year-aged shoyu tare. The flagship 特製 鶏パイタンらーめん comes with three kinds of chashu (rare pork shoulder, charcoal-grilled belly, thin-sliced loin), a soft-set egg made with Fukuchiyama eggs, and fried enoki mushrooms — a topping the shop bills as rare, possibly a first, in Kyoto.

anecdotes.text: Nakasawa runs the kitchen solo, preparing every bowl himself. A noodle-making machine sits visible from the street, reserved for his plan to eventually make the shop's own noodles in-house; for now the thin straight noodles come from Menya Teigyaku (棣鄂).
The fried enoki topping on the paitan bowl is promoted locally as a Kyoto first, alongside the unusual four-component 'quadruple' broth.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: magazine.tabelog.com profiles chef 中澤敬士 (36): born in Kyoto, moved to Toyama in middle school, ~18 years cooking ramen in Toyama and Tokyo, opened near Kinkakuji Oct 2023; the chicken-paitan uses a 'quadruple' base (京赤地鶏 chicken bones, pork bones, Lake Shinji shijimi, seafood) with 3-year-aged shoyu, charcoal chashu, Fukuchiyama egg, fried enoki, and 棣鄂 noodles, run solo. osumituki.com dates the opening to 2023-10-17, confirms the quadruple broth, the 特製 bowl's three chashu types, and fried enoki as a likely Kyoto first.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Bowls are dressed with a three-year-aged soy-sauce (shoyu) tare; soy sauce of this type is wheat-based, making the shoyu bowls unsuitable for gluten-free diners.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The single shared broth is an animal stock (chicken, pork, clam, fish); there is no separate vegetarian or vegan preparation, so no bowl can be made vegan.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, friendly solo-run counter shop where a few words of Japanese and a smile go a long way; English support is unlikely, so pointing and basic phrases are the comfortable way to order.

kyr_ramen_saishin.gf_detail: Standard ramen shop: wheat noodles served in pork/chicken broth with (typically wheat-based) shoyu or miso tare. No gluten-free noodles, dedicated prep, or allergen accommodation found in any source. Not suitable for celiacs.
kyr_ramen_saishin.vegan_detail: All bowls are built on a chicken-and-pork-bone (tori-tonkotsu) broth; toppings include chashu pork. No vegan or vegetarian ramen option is described. Not suitable for vegans.
kyr_ramen_saishin.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Fri, Sat 11:30-14:30 & 18:00-22:00; Wed 18:00-22:00; Thu 11:30-14:30 & 18:00-23:30; Sun closed. (Sources vary; some report later night hours to ~01:00-01:30. Irregular closures occur — check ahead.)
kyr_ramen_saishin.notes: [Mom & Pop] Ramen Saishin opened on February 19, 2017 in the Misonobashi area of Kyoto's Kita Ward, taking over the premises of a previous ramen shop called Ramen Akashin that had closed a month earlier. The new operation kept the predecessor's layout, giving the place the lived-in feel of a

chef_bio.origin: Kyoto (Kita-ku, near Kamigamo Shrine and Kyoto Sangyo University)
chef_bio.background: Ramen Saishin opened on February 19, 2017 in the Misonobashi area of Kyoto's Kita Ward, taking over the premises of a previous ramen shop called Ramen Akashin that had closed about a month earlier. The new operation kept the predecessor's layout, giving the place the lived-in feel of a long-established neighborhood shop, and inherited its taste and some recipes.
chef_bio.philosophy: Mellow, refined broths rather than heavy or aggressive richness — a simple, balanced bowl that locals describe as easy to finish, with thicker noodles paired to the miso and thinner noodles to the shoyu.
chef_bio.specialty: A chicken-and-pork-bone (tori-tonkotsu) ramen offered in shio (salt), shoyu (soy sauce), and miso versions. The salt bowl is notable for a smooth, pale, almost corn-potage-colored broth in which chicken umami leads over the pork-bone richness, served with medium-thin straight noodles, a single thick slice of charred chashu, menma, nori, bean sprouts and scallions.

anecdotes.text: The shop carried forward a peppery nira (Chinese chive) side dish inherited from the previous tenant, Ramen Akashin.

Run by two women, the counter is described as welcoming for solo diners, and it is a lunchtime favorite of nearby Kyoto Sangyo University students — fried-chicken (karaage) sets come with generous rice.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: osumituki.com confirms Saishin opened 2017-02-19 in Kita-ku's Misonobashi in the premises of Ramen Akashin (closed ~2017-01-19), kept the layout, inherited the taste and a peppery nira side, and serves tori-tonkotsu in shio/shoyu/miso with thicker noodles for miso and thinner for shoyu, near Kamigamo/Kyoto Sangyo University. kyoto-gourmet.info describes it as run by two women (女性2人), welcoming to solo diners, popular with Kyoto Sangyo students, with a pale corn-potage-colored chicken-forward salt broth (~700 yen), medium-thin noodles and one thick charred chashu slice.

cultural_comfort.note: A small neighborhood ramen counter run by local staff with a student clientele; little to no English is expected, so a few Japanese phrases or pointing at the menu will help.

kyr_imadegawa_mazesoba_sensh.gf_detail: This is a wheat-noodle mazesoba shop. The thick flat noodles are wheat-based, and the sweet-spicy tare is almost certainly soy-sauce-based (wheat-containing). There is no indication of any gluten-free option, dedicated equipment, or allergen accommodation. Not suitable for celiac or strict gluten-free diners.
kyr_imadegawa_mazesoba_sensh.vegan_detail: The standard bowl includes pork (肉), and the signature 戦車スペシャル adds extra pork plus fish powder (魚粉); a raw egg is also a standard topping. Toppings such as scallions, bean sprouts, garlic, and pickled ginger are plant-based, but the base dish and tare are not vegan and there is no advertised vegan option. Not suitable for vegans.
kyr_imadegawa_mazesoba_sensh.hours_raw: 11:30-15:00 (L.O. 14:45). Lunch-only operation inside a live-music venue basement. Operates roughly 20 days a month with irregular closures — check the shop's SNS for the day's status.
kyr_imadegawa_mazesoba_sensh.notes: [Mom & Pop] Opened October 2, 2021, this is the Kansai-region outpost of a mazesoba concept produced by Saitama's 大宮まぜそば誠治 (Omiya Mazesoba Seiji). It runs as a daytime tenant operation in the basement of a live-music venue (PUB VOXhall / ファーストコート御所室町) near Imadegawa-Karasuma, in the heart of

chef_bio.origin: Concept originates from Saitama (大宮まぜそば誠治); this is its first Kansai location.
chef_bio.background: Opened October 2, 2021, this is the Kansai-region outpost of a mazesoba concept produced by Saitama's 大宮まぜそば誠治 (Omiya Mazesoba Seiji). It runs as a daytime sub-tenant operation in the basement of a live-music venue (PUB VOXhall) near Imadegawa-Karasuma in Kamigyo ward, in the heart of the student district.
chef_bio.philosophy: Customization-first: a mild, sweet-savory sauce as a canvas, with 10-plus toppings and free add-ons (garlic, pickled ginger, oil, raw egg) so each diner builds their own bowl — staff even suggest trying it once without garlic to taste the sauce.
chef_bio.specialty: The signature bowl is the 戦車スペシャル (Sensha Special): the base mazesoba of flat thick wavy noodles from Menya Teigaku (麺屋棣鄂) tossed in a sweet-spicy tare, piled with extra pork (肉増し), chopped scallions (刻みネギ), and fish powder (魚粉), then finished with a 追い飯 rice refill so you can mop up the leftover sauce.

anecdotes.text: Diners crack a raw egg over the noodles and eat it sukiyaki-style, then add a rice refill to finish the remaining sauce.
It has reportedly become an unofficial campus cafeteria for nearby Doshisha University students.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: life-info.co.jp confirms Sensha is the Kansai debut of Saitama's 大宮まぜそば誠治, operating as a basement sub-tenant of PUB VOXhall near Imadegawa-Karasuma (Kamigyo-ku); signature 戦車スペシャル uses 麺屋棣鄂 noodles with 10+ toppings, a sukiyaki-style raw egg and a 追い飯 rice refill, and it has become popular with Doshisha University students (M 300g ¥1,040 / S 200g ¥800).

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The mazesoba is served in a sweet-spicy tare (甘辛いタレ); such tare is standard soy-sauce-based and wheat-containing, though the shop does not publish its ingredients.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Base bowl and signature special contain pork and fish powder, and raw egg is a standard add-on; no vegan preparation is described.

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny, cash-and-QR student-district lunch counter run in Japanese with no reservations and irregular hours — comfortable for an independent visitor who can order in Japanese and roll with a casual, no-frills setup.

kyr_zuishin.gf_detail: No gluten-free provision found. The signature bowls are built on wheat ramen noodles (and the crispy 揚げそば on fried wheat noodles) in chicken-and-seafood broth, with Chinese-style sauces that typically contain wheat-based soy sauce. Not suitable for celiacs.
kyr_zuishin.vegan_detail: Not a vegetarian or vegan venue. The kitchen centers on chicken-bone and seafood broth, pork gyoza, and meat/seafood Chinese dishes; no vegan ramen or confirmed plant-based options were found. A vegetable stir-fry (野菜炒め) appears on the menu but is not confirmed meat/animal-stock free.
kyr_zuishin.hours_raw: 11:30-15:00 (L.O. 14:30), 17:00-21:00 (L.O. 20:30); closed Tuesdays. (Some listings note lunch to 14:30 and dinner to 20:50.)
kyr_zuishin.notes: [Mom & Pop] Zuishin is a small, hard-to-find Chinese restaurant tucked deep within a quiet Yamashina residential neighborhood, reached through narrow back streets a short walk from Nagitsuji Station. Locals describe it as a hidden gem that carries the quiet confidence of a long-respected est

chef_bio.background: Zuishin is a small, hard-to-find Chinese restaurant tucked deep within a quiet Yamashina residential neighborhood (Nagitsuji-Nishiura), reached through narrow back streets about a 10-minute walk from Nagitsuji Station. Locals describe it as a hidden gem that carries the quiet confidence of a long-respected establishment, with a bright, energetic owner.
chef_bio.philosophy: The kitchen positions itself as authentic Chinese cooking (中国料理) rather than the Japanized 中華 stereotype, leaning on the aroma of its ingredients - for example gyoza scented with genuine star anise - rather than heavy seasoning.
chef_bio.specialty: The signature bowl is the tori-soba (chicken soba): a refined, clear (清湯) soup built on chicken-bone stock rounded out with seafood umami, pairing mellow body with a clean finish. Silky noodles are matched to the soup. The crispy fried noodles (揚げそば), made by deep-frying flat wide noodles for a fragrant crunch, and the curry fried rice are other house favorites.

anecdotes.text: Diners note the soup balances chicken-bone richness with added seafood umami for a flavor that is both mellow and crisp, with the tori-soba treated as the standout.
The crispy fried noodles are flat, wide noodles deep-fried until fragrant, served with vegetables and pork in sauce.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: osumituki.com places Zuishin in a hard-to-find residential street of Yamashina-ku (椥辻西浦町, ~10 min from Nagitsuji Station), serving authentic 中国料理: gyoza with genuine star anise (八角) aroma, delicate crispy 揚げそば (flat wide noodles), curry fried rice and ramen (~¥650), with a bright, energetic owner (name not published). The tori-soba clear soup and seafood-rounded chicken stock are treated as the standout.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Authentic Chinese dishes and tare here typically use wheat-based soy sauce; no wheat-free soy sauce is indicated.
soy_sauce_wheat.why: Soy-sauce warning invented from the genre label — the cited page contains zero evidence about seasoning, and the one tare the menu DOES name is 味噌 (味噌ラーメン), not 醤油. Repoint this citation at what the page actually proves: the gluten here is the wheat noodles (ラーメン, 中華やきそば, 揚げそば = deep-fried flat whea

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny neighborhood Chinese restaurant tucked deep in a Yamashina residential block; service is in Japanese and best approached with a guide or some Japanese, with simple points-and-smile ordering otherwise.

kyr_karamenya_shachirin_kyot.gf_detail: No gluten-free option. The bowls are built on wheat ramen noodles with a house chili tare (Japanese chili-pepper/soy tares are typically wheat-containing) over a meat broth, plus minced pork, chashu and back fat. There is no published allergen information and no dedicated handling, so this should be treated as unsafe for celiac diners. Expect wheat throughout.
kyr_karamenya_shachirin_kyot.vegan_detail: Not vegan-friendly. The signature spicy bowls are topped with stir-fried minced meat, seared chashu pork and pork back fat, finished with a beaten egg, over a meat-based broth. No vegetable or plant-based ramen is offered.
kyr_karamenya_shachirin_kyot.hours_raw: 11:30-15:00 (L.O. 14:45), 18:00-20:30 (L.O. 20:00). Closed every Tue and the 2nd and 4th Wed.
kyr_karamenya_shachirin_kyot.notes: [Mom & Pop] Shachirin opened on July 15, 2023 on Imadegawa near the Doshisha University campus, bringing the 'Nagoya karamen' style to Kyoto as a branch of the Nagoya brand 名古屋辛麺 鯱輪. The whole 11-seat counter shop leans into its theme — walls, chairs and towels are bright red, as if the room

chef_bio.background: Shachirin opened on July 15, 2023 on Imadegawa near the Doshisha University campus (about 5 minutes from Imadegawa subway station), bringing the 'Nagoya karamen' style to Kyoto as a branch of the Nagoya brand 名古屋辛麺 鯱輪. The whole 11-seat counter shop leans into its theme — walls, chairs and towels are bright red, as if the room itself were a bowl of spicy ramen.
chef_bio.philosophy: House-developed chili heat built on three kinds of chili pepper blended for sweetness, aroma and spiciness, prepared cup by cup, layered onto a savory umami base.
chef_bio.specialty: Its signature is the umami-spicy bowl (旨辛にんにくラーメン) that fuses Nagoya Taiwan-style ramen with Miyazaki karamen: stir-fried minced meat, garlic, Chinese chives, bean sprouts and green onion over noodles, with optional seared chashu and sweet back fat, and a beaten egg to mellow the heat. Diners pick a spice level from normal up through 5 and then several steps beyond, and many pour the leftover spicy soup over a free bowl of rice.

anecdotes.text: The recipe was supervised by Naoto Niiyama (新山直人), head (総大将) of the acclaimed Nagoya ramen shop Menya Hanabi (麺屋はなび), the shop credited with originating Taiwan mazesoba.
The interior is deliberately all-red — walls, chairs and towels — so the whole shop reads as a giant bowl of spicy ramen.
Noodle dishes come with free rice refills, and customers commonly finish by pouring the spicy broth over rice.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: leafkyoto.net confirms the Kyoto Imadegawa branch opened 2023-07-15, the all-red 11-seat room, the 3-chili blend, and roots in the Nagoya brand 名古屋辛麺 鯱輪. Official shachirin.com states the brand's flavor was supervised by 新山直人, the 総大将 of Taiwan-ramen originator 麺屋はなび, and describes the pork/chicken/vegetable base and Nagoya-Taiwan + Miyazaki-karamen fusion; osumituki.com confirms free rice refills.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Bowls are built on wheat ramen noodles in a shared spicy-ramen kitchen; no gluten-free preparation is mentioned (per Leaf Kyoto).

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The menu includes a soy-sauce ramen and a chili-based spicy tare; Japanese soy sauce and chili tares are typically wheat-containing, though the page does not list allergens (per Osumituki).

vegan_cross_contact.text: Signature bowls are topped with stir-fried minced meat, seared chashu pork, back fat and a beaten egg over a meat broth; no plant-based option is offered (per Leaf Kyoto).

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny 11-seat counter ramen bar with no English menu or allergen info; a knowledgeable guide is recommended, though a GF/vegan diner realistically cannot eat here.

kyr_menbaka_ichidai_menbaka_.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. ⚠ Safety review 2026-07-02: downgraded high→options. The 'pure wheat, no GF' prior is wrong — a real GF program exists (rice-flour noodles, GF soy sauce tare, dedicated pots/utensils on request; multiple celiac reviewers report safe visits). Too much substance for 'no.' BUT doesn't clear 'high': printed menu reportedly says GF noodles boiled in the SAME water as wheat noodles then rinsed (not celiac-safe), safe handling conditional on declaring celiac, staff-vs-menu accounts conflict. Single small tourist kitchen, not dedicated. Open. — Prior note: The shop's official site states it serves gluten-sensitive guests using premium rice-flour noodles and dedicated pots and utensils "to minimize cross-contamination." This is a genuine, intentional gluten-free offering — unusual for a ramen shop, where noodles, shoyu tare and broth are normally wheat-based. However, it is not a dedicated gluten-free kitchen, and the GF/vegan special bowls must be booked in advance via the TableCheck reservation (the reservation-only "special set menu"); the regular walk-in menu is standard wheat ramen. Highly sensitive celiacs should reserve the GF set, state their needs clearly, and confirm cross-contamination handling on arrival.
kyr_menbaka_ichidai_menbaka_.vegan_detail: A full vegan version of the fire ramen has been offered since 2020: a plant-based soy-sauce soup with no animal broth, custom firm noodles, and tofu/vegetable substitutions, plus vegan sides such as gyoza and karaage (mock meat). Vegan orders are tracked with a colored number card at the seat. The vegan bowls are part of the reservation-only special set menu, so book ahead via TableCheck rather than relying on walk-in.
kyr_menbaka_ichidai_menbaka_.hours_raw: 11:00-21:00 daily (Tabelog/official). Lunch service approx 11:00-15:30 and dinner approx 17:00-21:00 per the official reservation page; the kitchen notes the meal takes considerably longer than a typical ramen shop due to the fire performance.

chef_bio.background: Founded in 1984 in Kyoto, this counter ramen shop began serving conventional bowls before its owner stumbled onto the idea that would make it world-famous. Working with Kyoto's prized Kujo green onions, he sought a way to keep the noodles screaming-hot while showcasing a mound of fresh raw scallions on top.
chef_bio.philosophy: Treat ramen as both craft and spectacle: preserve traditional Kyoto shoyu ramen flavor while turning each serving into a joyful, memorable performance, and welcome guests from everywhere — the shop states it offers vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free and Muslim-friendly (no-pork) options prepared with the same care.
chef_bio.specialty: Negi Ramen, better known as Fire Ramen: a light yet deeply savory chicken-and-seafood soy-sauce broth piled with fresh Kujo scallions, finished tableside when the cook pours scallion oil heated past 300 degrees Celsius over the bowl. The oil ignites into a column of flame that chars the onions, drawing out their sweetness and aroma while keeping the bowl piping hot.

anecdotes.text: The flames are not just theater: scallion oil heated above 300C throws up a pillar of fire that chars the Kujo onions and keeps the bowl scalding hot. After a 2019 renovation the counter was rebuilt with fire-resistant stainless-steel seating, and staff give a safety briefing and paper aprons before lighting each bowl.

About a year after opening the founder discovered that pouring flaming oil over freshly chopped green onions produced an extraordinary aroma and flavor, and that discovery became the shop's signature Fire Ramen.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Official fireramen.com credits founder Masamichi Miyazawa, dates the shop to 1984 near Nijo Castle, describes Fire Ramen's shoyu base and the ~1-year-after-opening discovery of flaming scallion oil, and lists stated vegan/vegetarian/gluten-free/Muslim-friendly options (dietary safety not independently asserted). livejapan.com confirms the 300C+ scallion oil, the flame pillar that chars Kujo scallions, the 2019 stainless-steel renovation, the safety briefing and paper aprons, and the chicken-and-seafood soy broth.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The shop says it uses dedicated pots and utensils to minimize cross-contamination for gluten-free guests, but it is a shared kitchen that also cooks standard wheat ramen, so it is not a fully dedicated gluten-free environment.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The regular menu is a soy-sauce (shoyu) ramen; standard shoyu tare is typically wheat-based. The gluten-free version is a separate reservation-only preparation rather than the default bowl.
soy_sauce_wheat.why: First half supported. Second half is CONTRADICTED by the same page: the Walk in Course Menu, not only the two reservation courses, is labelled '（Vegetarian, Muslim friendly, Gluten free available）'. GF is not reservation-only. The record also omits that the FMGF owner statement says GF bowls use glu

vegan_cross_contact.text: Vegan orders are marked with a colored number card placed at the seat so staff serve the correct plant-based bowl, but the shop does not publish details on separate cooking surfaces for vegan items.
vegan_cross_contact.source_wording: "When you order the vegan menu, a green number card is placed in front of your seat to ensure flawless service for those who have chosen the vegan option."

staff_allergy_handling.text: Gluten-free, vegan, vegetarian and no-pork (Muslim-friendly) bowls are offered as a reservation-only special set menu booked in advance via TableCheck; the regular walk-in menu cannot be swapped for these, so dietary guests should reserve ahead and state needs clearly.
staff_allergy_handling.why: MATERIAL MISREADING of the cited sentence. The site means a RESERVATION cannot be downgraded to the regular menu — not that dietary bowls require a reservation. The page marks the Walk in Course Menu as Vegetarian/Muslim-friendly/Gluten-free available, and an FMGF reviewer describes walking in witho

positives.text: Rare among ramen shops, this kitchen intentionally caters to gluten-free, vegan, vegetarian and Muslim-friendly diners, with premium rice-flour noodles for gluten-free guests and a fully plant-based vegan fire ramen offered since 2020.
English website, English-speaking staff and online reservations make it straightforward for foreign diners to arrange and confirm special dietary bowls before visiting.

Greg set "options" on 2026-08-23 after the sweep found the gluten-free bowl is a reservation-only preparation booked in advance via TableCheck, while the regular walk-in menu is a wheat-based shoyu ramen. "high" would read as safe to someone who walks in off the street, which is the common case for this shop.

cultural_comfort.note: This is a famous tourist-facing spot with an English-language website, English-speaking staff, online reservations (TableCheck) and printed safety/allergy guidance, so foreign visitors are very comfortable here.

Too much substance for 'no.' BUT doesn't clear 'high': printed menu reportedly says GF noodles boiled in the SAME water as wheat noodles then rinsed (not celiac-safe), safe handling conditional on declaring celiac, staff-vs-menu accounts conflict. Single small tourist kitchen, not dedicated. Open.

safe protocol only triggered if you declare celiac; default is shared water
conflicting menu-vs-staff accounts, no written guarantee
single small non-dedicated high-throughput tourist kitchen
gf_review.plain_rice: GF fried rice available (made with GF soy); plain steamed white rice not explicitly documented

kyr_men_to_sake_no_tora.gf_detail: A tantanmen specialist built on wheat ramen noodles (the soup-less version uses thick flat crimped wheat noodles), a Sichuan sesame-and-ground-pork sauce, and chili/Sichuan-pepper seasonings. No gluten-free noodle or tare option is mentioned anywhere, and tantanmen of this style is essentially never celiac-safe. Treat as not gluten-free.
kyr_men_to_sake_no_tora.vegan_detail: A meat-forward shop: the signature bowls center on a ground-pork/meat-miso (肉味噌) topping and a rich creamy sesame broth, and side dishes include beef tataki, gyoza, and fried chicken. No vegan or vegetarian tantanmen is advertised. Not suitable for vegans.
kyr_men_to_sake_no_tora.hours_raw: 11:00-15:00 / 17:00-20:00 (lunch and dinner service daily; closing days irregular)
kyr_men_to_sake_no_tora.notes: [Mom & Pop] Tucked down a side street just west of Higashioji-dori between Imadegawa and Higashi-ichijo, a short walk from Demachiyanagi and Kyoto University, this little tantanmen counter occupies a space that used to be a neighborhood sake shop with a standing-drink corner. It was reborn i

chef_bio.background: Tucked down a side street just west of Higashioji-dori between Imadegawa and Higashi-ichijo, a short walk from Demachiyanagi and Kyoto University, this little tantanmen counter occupies a space that used to be a neighborhood sake shop with a standing-drink corner. It was reborn in May 2025, reworked under the guidance of Kinshiro (金鵄楼), a Gosho-minami tantanmen specialist that drew lines soon after it opened in 2024.
chef_bio.philosophy: True to its name 'Noodles and Sake' (麺と酒の寅), the place is built around the idea of 'have a drink, then close the night with a bowl of tantanmen' — a casual student-and-local hangout where you tune your own bowl by circling choices on a paper order slip (noodle firmness, scallions, scallion oil, fried onion, meat miso, chili-oil heat, and how much Sichuan pepper).
chef_bio.specialty: Sichuan-style tantanmen in two forms: a rich, creamy soup version and a soup-less (mazesoba-style) version built on thick, flat, crimped wheat noodles that grab the sauce. The flavor leans on a fragrant sesame base lifted by the tingle of Sichuan pepper (huajiao), with a meat-miso topping blended for a deeper, more layered umami than the parent shop.

anecdotes.text: The shop is a Kinshiro-supervised spinoff; rather than copy the parent, it deliberately uses thick flat crimped noodles for the soup-less bowl and a re-blended meat miso to create its own deeper, more complex flavor.

The concept is 'a drink first, then finish with tantanmen' (一杯やって担担麺で〆る), aimed in part at the nearby Kyoto University student crowd, with beef tataki, gyoza, and karaage to go with the sake before the noodles.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotopi.jp confirms the shop opened May 2025 in a former Yoshida (Sakyo-ku) sake shop with a standing-drink counter near Kyoto University, supervised by Gosho-minami tantanmen specialist 金鵄楼 (Kinshiro, opened 2024, quickly popular); it serves soup and soup-less Sichuan tantanmen with thick flat crimped noodles and a re-blended, more complex meat miso, paper-slip customization (firmness, negi, scallion oil, fried onion, meat miso, chili oil, Sichuan pepper), the '一杯やって担担麺で〆る' concept, ~16 seats, and sides of beef tataki, gyoza and karaage.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, student-friendly local noodle counter where you order by circling options on a paper slip, so basic Japanese (or pointing) makes ordering much smoother; no English service is advertised.

kyr_kirin_en_2.gf_detail: No gluten-free provision is published. The signature dish is wheat-noodle tantanmen, and the kitchen is a full Chinese restaurant relying on wheat-based soy sauce, broths and house-made meat miso. The hallmark heat comes from chili blends, not from any allergen-controlled prep. A celiac diner should treat this as unsafe; no dedicated equipment or GF menu is indicated.
kyr_kirin_en_2.vegan_detail: This is a meat-and-seafood Chinese restaurant. The famous tantanmen is built on a house-made pork "meat miso" (自家製肉味噌) over a chicken-bone (鶏ガラ) broth, and other signatures include black-vinegar sweet-and-sour pork. No vegan ramen or vegan menu is advertised; a vegan diner would need to ask, with little to expect.
kyr_kirin_en_2.hours_raw: Lunch 11:00-14:00, Dinner 16:30-22:00 (official site lists dinner to 23:00 / L.O. 22:30). Closed Tuesdays (next business day if Tuesday is a holiday).
kyr_kirin_en_2.notes: [Mom & Pop] Kirin-en opened in 1967 (Showa 42), when the area around Mukocho was still mostly farmland and authentic Chinese food was a rarity. The founder set out, in his words, to let the people of Mukocho enjoy real Cantonese cooking, and the place has carried on as a family-run restauran

chef_bio.background: Kirin-en opened in 1967 (Showa 42), when the area around Mukocho was still mostly farmland and authentic Chinese food was a rarity. The founder set out, in his words, to let the people of Mukocho enjoy real Cantonese cooking, and the place has carried on as a family-run restaurant ever since, today led by Tamotsu Miyaji (宮路保) with manager Ryo Miyaji (宮路亮).
chef_bio.philosophy: Their stated aim with the famous bowl was not heat for its own sake but 美味くて辛い - delicious AND spicy - with a spectrum running from mild to brutally hot so anyone can find their level.
chef_bio.specialty: The house gekikara (extreme-spice) tantanmen: a chili blend once built around jolokia, then famed as the world's hottest pepper, layered over a house-made pork meat-miso for body and a chicken-bone broth finished with sesame for depth. It won the Gold Grand Prix at the very first KARA-1 contest. Beyond the noodles, the owner's own favorite is the black-vinegar sweet-and-sour pork, made with traditional bottle-fermented black vinegar prized by regulars.

anecdotes.text: The tantanmen was born out of Mukocho's community-revitalization push that became the Kyoto Gekikara (extreme-spice) shopping street; Kirin-en's bowl took the inaugural KARA-1 Gold Grand Prix.
Founder's recollection that he resolved to bring authentic Cantonese cuisine to Mukocho residents back when the neighborhood was largely farmland.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: otokuni-kyoto.sakura.ne.jp confirms Kirin-en opened 1967 (Showa 42) in Mukocho when it was largely farmland, with the founder's mission to bring authentic Cantonese cooking; the family business is led by 宮路保 (representative) and 宮路亮 (manager); the jolokia-based gekikara tantanmen (with house meat-miso and sesame-finished chicken-bone broth) won the inaugural KARA-1 Gold Grand Prix, and the black-vinegar sweet-and-sour pork is a signature. Near JR Mukomachi / Hankyu Higashi-Mukо station.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: As a full Chinese restaurant, dishes rely on standard (wheat-based) soy sauce and seasonings; no wheat-free tare or sauce is indicated.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The signature tantanmen is built on house-made pork meat-miso over a chicken-bone broth, so shared pots and broths make vegan separation impractical.

cultural_comfort.note: A long-running, family-run neighborhood Chinese restaurant with a roomy tatami second floor and no English noted, so a little guidance on ordering and on the spice scale helps.

kyr_aji_no_tentoku_kyoto_shi.gf_detail: Not celiac-safe. Abura soba is built on wheat noodles tossed in a soy-based tare (Japanese soy sauce almost always contains wheat). The "plant-based oil" point refers to the dressing oil being vegetable oil rather than lard — it has nothing to do with gluten. There is no indication of gluten-free noodles, dedicated prep, or allergen handling. Gluten-avoiders should not eat here.
kyr_aji_no_tentoku_kyoto_shi.vegan_detail: Not vegan. Despite using plant-based (vegetable) oil rather than animal fat, the standard bowl is topped with chashu (pork) and the soy-based tare typically contains animal-derived components. No vegan/vegetarian version is advertised. The "healthier plant oil" framing is a marketing point about fat type, not a plant-based menu. A vegan diner could ask whether a no-chashu bowl is possible, but the tare itself is not confirmed plant-based, so it cannot be recommended as vegan.
kyr_aji_no_tentoku_kyoto_shi.hours_raw: Mon-Fri 18:00-23:00 / Sat, Sun 17:30-23:00, irregular days off
kyr_aji_no_tentoku_kyoto_shi.notes: [Mom & Pop] Aji no Tentoku is an abura soba specialist chain originating in Kanagawa (Kakio main shop), operated by Tenki Co., Ltd. In Kyoto it has the Shijo Kiyamachi shop and the Gion shop; the Shijo Kiyamachi shop is a small counter shop along the Takase River, a very short walk from Hankyu Kyoto-Kawaramachi Station in a corner of the entertainment district.

chef_bio.origin: 運営は株式会社天輝（油そば味の天徳ブランド、関東発・京都進出）
chef_bio.background: 味の天徳は神奈川（柿生本店）発祥の油そば専門チェーンで、株式会社天輝が運営する。京都には四条木屋町店と祇園店を構え、四条木屋町店は下京区真町、阪急京都河原町駅から徒歩すぐの繁華街にあるカウンター8席ほどの小さな店。
chef_bio.philosophy: 油そばを『第三の麺類』と位置づけ、動物性の脂ではなく植物性の油を使うことでヘルシーさを打ち出している点が京都での売り。客が酢・ラー油で自分好みに仕上げる参加型の一杯。
chef_bio.specialty: 看板は油そば。中太のちょい縮れ麺を醤油ベースのタレと植物油で和えたスープのない一杯で、メンマ・ねぎ・刻み海苔・チャーシューがのる。途中で酢とラー油を加えて味変し『二度美味しい』のが定番の食べ方。醤油だれと塩だれが選べる。

anecdotes.text: 『京都初の油そば専門店』をうたい、植物性の油を使うためあっさり食べられると紹介されている。
途中から酢とラー油を足して二度美味しい、というのが店の定番の食べ方として案内されている。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 株式会社天輝の公式店舗ページで運営会社・神奈川柿生本店発祥・京都四条木屋町/祇園店の存在を確認。Rettyで『途中から酢とラー油を足して二度美味しい油そば』の食べ方を、ぐるぱす等で『京都初の油そば専門店・植物性の油使用』の標榜を確認。店主名は非公開のためnull。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Core dish is wheat abura soba noodles dressed in a soy-based tare; no gluten-free option or allergen separation indicated anywhere.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The abura soba uses a 醤油ベース (soy-sauce-based) tare; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Standard bowl is topped with chashu (pork); no vegan/vegetarian preparation is advertised.

positives.text: Uses plant-based (vegetable) oil rather than animal fat in the dressing — a lighter-fat bowl, though this does not make it gluten-free or vegan.

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny, cash-only counter abura soba shop where ordering is simple but staff likely speak little English and there is no allergen support, so basic Japanese and self-direction help.

kyr_ryouriya_terado.gf_detail: Not safe for celiacs. The noodles are wheat (the curry tsukemen broth is also thickened to a heavy wheat-flour consistency), and a kappo kitchen serving sashimi, sake, and grilled fish relies on standard wheat-based soy sauce and seasonings. There is no dedicated gluten-free menu or any stated allergen accommodation.
kyr_ryouriya_terado.vegan_detail: No vegan offering. This is a Japanese kappo whose signature noodle dish is a curry tsukemen built on a bonito (katsuobushi) dashi and served with chicken and egg; the broth, tare, and toppings are animal-based, and the evening menu centers on sashimi and fish. Nothing on the menu is plant-based by design, and there is no indication staff can prepare a vegan version.
kyr_ryouriya_terado.hours_raw: 17:00-22:00. Closed Mondays. (Note: a daytime curry tsukemen has historically been offered, but the official site currently describes the shop as a dinner-only, reservation-based kappo with very limited seatings; lunch availability is uncertain.)
kyr_ryouriya_terado.notes: A small owner-run Japanese kappo on Tominokoji just north of Shijo, a few minutes from Kawaramachi. It opened in December 2019 in a space that had previously housed the curry-tsukemen specialist Menya Itadori (麺屋虎杖), which closed at the end of September 2019. After a temporary cl

chef_bio.background: A small owner-run Japanese kappo on Tominokoji just north of Shijo in Shimogyo Ward, a few minutes from Kawaramachi. It opened in December 2019 in a space that had previously housed the curry-tsukemen specialist Menya Itadori (麺屋虎杖), which closed at the end of September 2019, and it continues to operate today.
chef_bio.philosophy: The owner frames the place around wholehearted Kyoto hospitality (真心込めて、おもてなし) and lively, enjoyable time shared with family and friends ('てら戸でご家族や友人と一緒に賑やかで楽しい時間をお過ごしください').
chef_bio.specialty: By night it is a kappo for sashimi, grilled fish, and sushi paired with sake and shochu; its signature crossover dish is a curry tsukemen whose dipping broth is built on a strong katsuobushi (bonito) dashi so the Japanese dashi flavor holds its own against the sweet, old-soba-shop-style curry, finished with aonori and served with thick noodles, summer vegetables, chicken, and a soft egg.

anecdotes.text: The shop carried on the curry-tsukemen lineage of the address: the previous tenant was Menya Itadori, a curry tsukemen specialty shop that closed on September 30, 2019, and Terado opened the following December offering its own kappo take on the dish.

What makes the bowl distinctive is the deliberate balance of a heavily bonito-forward Japanese dashi against a sweet, aonori-dusted curry, an intentionally kappo-minded reworking of a casual lunch noodle.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト(ryouriya-terado.com)で店主『寺戸 昌規』と『ご家族や友人と賑やかで楽しい時間を』というもてなしのコンセプトを確認。osumitukiで前テナント麺屋虎杖(2019/9/30閉店)、2019年12月開業、鰹出汁の効いたカレーつけ麺(青のり・夏野菜・鶏・半熟卵)を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: The signature noodles are wheat and the curry dipping broth is described as having a thick wheat-flour consistency.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: A kappo serving sashimi and grilled fish; no wheat-free soy sauce or seasoning is indicated, so standard wheat-based soy sauce should be assumed.
soy_sauce_wheat.why: Genre inference wearing a citation. The source says nothing about soy sauce, and 'grilled fish' is not on it either. The page's real, quotable wheat hazard is the curry itself (小麦粉多め) — cite that. Either drop this entry or restate it honestly as an assumption with no source. Shop is trading: officia

cultural_comfort.note: A small owner-run kappo with counter seating and reservation-based, limited daily seatings; comfortable for a guest who can manage basic Japanese, with no indication of English support.

kyr_aburasoba_mazesoba_roman.gf_detail: Not celiac-safe. The signature bowls use house-made whole-wheat (全粒粉入り) thick noodles and a special shoyu tare, both wheat-based, with no gluten-free noodle or tare option found. The kitchen is built around these noodles, so cross-contact is unavoidable. Not suitable for anyone with celiac disease or a wheat allergy.
kyr_aburasoba_mazesoba_roman.vegan_detail: Not vegan-friendly. Abura soba and maze soba are built on a meat-based formula — chashu pork, spicy minced meat, soft-boiled or raw egg yolk, and a shoyu tare with oil/fish dashi notes. No vegan or vegetable-only bowl was found. A plant-based diner would have no safe main dish here.
kyr_aburasoba_mazesoba_roman.notes: A Kyoto outpost of the Osaka-born abura soba and maze soba specialist Roman (株式会社ロマン), this shop opened on May 16, 2022 along Imagawa-dori in the Hyakumanben district, a short walk from Kyoto University. Oil noodles and mixed noodles were still relatively uncommon in Kyoto at the

chef_bio.origin: Branch of the Osaka-headquartered Roman brand (parent company 株式会社ロマン, founded November 2020, HQ in Higashinari-ku, Osaka), which has grown to more than a dozen locations across Osaka and Kyoto.
chef_bio.background: A Kyoto outpost of the Osaka-born abura soba and maze soba specialist Roman (株式会社ロマン), this shop opened on May 16, 2022 along Imadegawa-dori in the Hyakumanben district, a short walk from Kyoto University. Oil noodles and mixed noodles were still relatively uncommon in Kyoto at the time, which made the new student-friendly counter a notable arrival in the neighborhood.
chef_bio.philosophy: The brand's stated belief is 'シンプルだからこその素材の味を大事にしています' — because the dish is simple, the flavor of the ingredients matters most. That focus shows in the whole-wheat (全粒粉) thick noodles the brand uses for its noodles.
chef_bio.specialty: Abura soba (brothless oil noodles) and maze soba — thick noodles tossed with a special shoyu tare and seasoned oil. The abura soba comes piled with chashu, menma, soft-boiled egg, and nori; the maze soba layers spicy minced meat, chives, green onion, bamboo shoots, and egg yolk over the same noodles. Diners add vinegar and the house chili oil and mix everything vigorously before eating.

anecdotes.text: The shop courts its Kyoto University neighbors directly with a student discount, and noodle portions scale up through 大盛・ダブル・トリプル all the way to a 'challenge' size.
An opening promotion gave the first 50 customers each day a free large portion or topping through the launch week (until May 22, 2022).

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: osumitukiで2022/5/16開業・左京区百万遍(今出川通沿い、京大近く)・大阪発の油そばまぜそば専門店・学割・大盛〜チャレンジまでの増量・先着50名無料キャンペーン(〜5/22)を確認。roman-japan公式で『シンプルだからこその素材の味を大事にしています』の理念と全粒粉太麺、company頁で創業2020年11月・大阪本社を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: The kitchen centers on house-made whole-wheat thick noodles boiled in shared water, so wheat cross-contact is unavoidable throughout.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Both signature bowls are dressed with a special shoyu (soy sauce) tare, which is wheat-based and a core component of the dish.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bowls include chashu pork, spicy minced meat, and egg, with shared utensils and prep surfaces; no plant-based preparation is offered.

cultural_comfort.note: A casual, fast-paced student noodle counter near Kyoto University where a few words of Japanese and pointing at the menu get you through ordering comfortably.

kyr_chuka_soba_hiro.gf_detail: Not celiac-safe. The bowls are wheat ramen noodles (flat medium-thick) in a pork-bone shoyu broth, and soy sauce (containing wheat) is central to both the tare and the recommended free-rice topping. No gluten-free menu, no separate preparation, and no gluten-free claims appear on any page. A celiac or gluten-avoidant diner cannot eat the ramen here.
kyr_chuka_soba_hiro.vegan_detail: Not suitable for vegans. The single broth style is pork-bone soy (豚骨醤油), and toppings/condiments revolve around chashu (pork belly), boiled egg, and meat-based components. No vegan or vegetarian option is offered or mentioned. Wakame, menma, and green onion exist as toppings but the broth itself is animal-based.
kyr_chuka_soba_hiro.notes: [Mom & Pop] Chuka Soba Hiro is a morning-ramen shop that opened March 28, 2026, in the redeveloping Kyoto Station / Hachijoguchi area. Known as the sister shop of the popular 'Ramen Hiro' in Saiin, its entrance is set deep in an alley to the left of the building.

chef_bio.origin: 京都・西院の本店「尋」の流れを汲む姉妹店。
chef_bio.background: 中華そば 尋（ひろ）は、2026年3月28日、再開発が進む京都駅・八条口エリアにオープンした朝ラーメンの店。西院で人気の「ラーメン 尋」の姉妹店として知られ、ビル左手の路地奥に入口を構える。
chef_bio.philosophy: 朝7時から開け、一杯ごとにごはんを無料で添える——朝ラーを気軽に楽しんでもらうための、気前のよいもてなしを大切にしている。
chef_bio.specialty: 看板は一杯の中華そば。澄んだ黄金色のクリアな豚骨醤油スープで、豚骨の力強い旨味を感じさせつつ塩分や醤油感は控えめに仕立て、朝に食べても重くならない一杯に仕上げている。麺は高加水の平打ち中太麺で、ぷりっとした弾力と滑らかな喉ごしが特徴。チャーシューは注文ごとに切り出す豚バラで、薄切り・厚切りの食感を楽しめる。

anecdotes.text: おすすめの食べ方は、無料のごはんにチャーシューとおろしにんにくをのせ、醤油をひと回し。卓上にはおろしにんにく・一味・醤油・きゅうりの漬物が用意されている。
メニューは中華そば・チャーシュー麺・わかめ中華そばの3種。基本トッピングはわかめ・メンマ・ねぎ・ゆで卵。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotopiで2026/3/28開業・京都駅八条口圏(南区西九条池ノ内町)・西院『ラーメン尋』の姉妹店・7:00開店・ラーメン1杯につきごはん無料・黄金色の澄んだ豚骨醤油・高加水の平打ち中太麺・3種メニュー(中華そば/チャーシュー麺/わかめ)・ごはん+チャーシュー+にんにくの食べ方を確認。店主名は非公開でnull。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat ramen noodles are the base of every bowl and are boiled in shared water; there is no gluten-free option or separate preparation noted.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The broth is a pork-bone shoyu (豚骨醤油) tare, and soy sauce is also part of the recommended free-rice topping and the tabletop condiments — soy sauce in Japan typically contains wheat.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The single broth is animal-based (pork bone), prepared alongside chashu (pork belly) and egg toppings; no vegan preparation exists.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, casual ticket-machine (食券制) morning-ramen counter where a few words of Japanese and a friendly greeting go a long way; no English service is indicated.

kyr_tonkotsu_gyokai_ramen_mi.gf_detail: Not safe for celiacs. The signature bowls are built on self-made wheat noodles, and a pork-bone-and-fish (tonkotsu gyokai) ramen of this style almost always uses a wheat-based shoyu tare. No gluten-free option is advertised and no allergen handling is described.
kyr_tonkotsu_gyokai_ramen_mi.vegan_detail: Not vegan-friendly. The entire concept is a heavy pork-bone (uses Niwa Kogen pork) and fish/dried-sardine broth with chashu pork toppings; there is no plant-based bowl.
kyr_tonkotsu_gyokai_ramen_mi.notes: [Mom & Pop] The owner is a graduate of the celebrated Kyoto ramen house Raamen Touhichi (らぁ麺とうひち), a Michelin Bib Gourmand name, where he is described as the first disciple and trained for around seven years. He went on to serve as manager at Raamen Suguru (らぁ麺すぐる), then deepened his craft o

chef_bio.background: The owner trained at the celebrated Kyoto ramen house Raamen Touhichi (らぁ麺とうひち), a Michelin Bib Gourmand name. He went on to serve as manager (店長) at Raamen Suguru (らぁ麺すぐる), then broadened his craft outside ramen at the yakiniku restaurant Nanzan (南山) before opening Minoru on his own on May 18, 2026 in Ichijoji, Sakyo-ku.
chef_bio.philosophy: He values handmade quality, making his own noodles and using domestically sourced ingredients where he can. He is confident enough in the seasoning balance that no table condiments are offered, asking guests to taste the bowl as built.
chef_bio.specialty: The signature is a rich-yet-mellow tonkotsu-gyokai (pork-bone and seafood) ramen at 1,100 yen with 180g of house-made medium-thick straight noodles, alongside tsukemen at 1,300 yen with 250g of noodles. A special ramen (1,500 yen) tops the bowl with four kinds of chashu made from Niwa Kogen (丹羽高原) pork, plus seasoned egg and extra charred nori.

anecdotes.text: It quickly became one of 2026's talked-about new Kyoto ramen openings, the proprietor opening 満を持して (with great anticipation) after his time at Touhichi.
The L-shaped open-kitchen counter (about 10 seats) gives a live-cooking feel, and the broth shows layered umami — 'ガツンと来る豚の凝縮された旨味' — over a calm, Japanese-style counter with no table condiments.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: gcjapanで『らぁ麺とうひち出身の店主』、2026/5/18開業、ラーメン1100円/180g・つけ麺1300円/250g・特製1500円で丹羽高原豚の4種チャーシューを確認。kyotopiで経歴(とうひち出身→らぁ麺すぐる店長→焼肉南山→独立)、卓上調味料なし、L字カウンター約10席のオープンキッチン、厚みのある旨味のスープを確認。『一番弟子』『約7年』の記載は両ソースになく削除。

gf_cross_contamination.text: House-made wheat noodles are central to every bowl, so a shared boiling pot and wheat-laden kitchen make cross-contamination effectively unavoidable for a celiac.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No tare/seasoning ingredients are published, but a tonkotsu-gyokai ramen of this style almost always relies on a wheat-based shoyu tare; assume the seasoning contains wheat unless confirmed otherwise.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Broth is built on pork bone and fish/dried sardine and toppings are pork chashu, so there is no plant-based preparation and animal products are throughout the kitchen.

positives.text: Noodles are made in-house and the shop emphasizes handmade quality and domestic ingredients, so staff know their components well even though no formal allergy program is described.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, newly opened counter ramen shop where ordering in basic Japanese is easiest; no English support is indicated.

kyr_nakamura_shoten_kyoto_ra.gf_detail: No gluten-free options. This is a classic ramen shop: wheat noodles in a chicken-and-seafood shio broth, with a salt tare that almost certainly contains wheat-based soy sauce/seasonings. No gluten-free noodles, dedicated preparation, or allergen accommodation is advertised on the shop's pages. Not suitable for celiac diners.
kyr_nakamura_shoten_kyoto_ra.vegan_detail: No vegan options. Every bowl is built on animal-based broth — chicken bones, whole chicken, kombu, and dried sardines (niboshi) — and topped with chashu pork. There is no plant-based ramen on the menu.

The group has spent decades refining chicken-and-seafoo

chef_bio.origin: Takatsuki, Osaka (Kinsei group); Kyoto Station branch
chef_bio.background: Nakamura Shoten is one of the ramen brands of the Kinsei group, founded in Takatsuki, Osaka on November 8, 2001 as 彩色ラーメンきんせい ('colorful ramen Kinsei') — named for the wish to make vividly colored ramen that shines like Venus in the night sky. The group has spent decades refining chicken-and-seafood broths and handmade noodles, and its Nakamura Shoten line carries that work into Kyoto. This branch sits on the 10th-floor Ramen Koji of the Kyoto Station Building.
chef_bio.philosophy: The group builds each bowl around a carefully balanced broth and handmade noodles, with a stated aim of bringing smiles and comfort through a single bowl of ramen ('ラーメンで笑顔に').
chef_bio.specialty: 金の塩 ('gold salt') — a clear, golden shio bowl built on chicken umami and Japanese dashi, given a refined ('お上品') presentation. The menu also runs to chicken-forward and chuka soba bowls; this is Takatsuki-style ramen 'where you can fully savor Japan's distinctive dashi'.

anecdotes.text: The parent brand was founded on November 8, 2001 in Takatsuki with the wish to create 'ramen as vividly colored as Venus shining in the night sky' ('夜空に輝く金星のような鮮やかな色のラーメンを創りたい') — the origin of the 'colorful ramen' (彩色) name.
At the group's Takatsuki home, the 金の塩 is praised for a light, clear chicken-bone broth ('あっさり！鶏ガラの旨味がよいですね！') and a refined, 'お上品' presentation — counter-only and queued at lunch.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kinseigroup公式historyで彩色ラーメンきんせいの創業=平成13年(2001)11月8日・高槻市栄町、『金星のような鮮やかな色のラーメンを創りたい』という店名由来、自家製麺・鶏塩の先駆けを確認。takatsuki-scrambleで金の塩(黄金色・鶏ガラのあっさり・お上品・カウンターのみ・昼は行列)を、京都駅ビル拉麺小路頁で10F出店・『だしを存分に味わえる大阪高槻ラーメン』・看板金の塩を確認。旧引用vacanは410 Goneのため差し替え。

cultural_comfort.note: A busy station food-court ramen counter where ordering is typically done at a ticket machine and a few words of Japanese plus pointing will carry you through comfortably.

kyr_ramen_makisada.gf_detail: Standard ramen profile: wheat straight thin noodles, a soy-sauce (typically wheat-based shoyu) tare, and an animal-based broth. No gluten-free accommodation is indicated; not suitable for celiac diners.
kyr_ramen_makisada.vegan_detail: The single ramen is an animal-based (dōbutsu-kei) shoyu broth topped with thin-sliced pork chāshū; the side shumai are pork. No vegan or vegetarian option is indicated.
kyr_ramen_makisada.notes: [Mom & Pop] Ramen Makisada is a ramen specialist opened April 27, 2026, at Takakura-dori Nijo Nishi-iru in Nakagyo Ward, close to Karasuma Oike, created by 'Kyo-Chuka Makisada,' a renowned creative-Chinese establishment in Kyoto. A small shop with only 10 calm counter seats reminiscent of a kappo restaurant, its signature bowl is a ground-up reconstruction as ramen of the negi soba that was originally served as a staff meal at Makisada.

chef_bio.origin: 京都・中京区。母体である「京中華 牧定」の系譜を受け継ぐ新店。
chef_bio.background: ラーメン まきさだは、烏丸御池からほど近い中京区高倉通二条西入に2026年4月27日にオープンした、京都の創作中華の名店「京中華 牧定」が手がけるラーメン専門店。割烹を思わせる落ち着いたカウンター10席のみの小さな店で、看板の一杯はもともと牧定でまかないとして振る舞われていたネギそばを、ラーメンとして一から再構築したもの。
chef_bio.philosophy: 店主は世代を超えて愛される地域の店を目指している――「幼い頃に親に連れられて来ていた子どもが、大人になって今度は自分の家族を連れて来る。そんなふうに世代を超えて愛され、地域に根付いた店にしたい」と語る。
chef_bio.specialty: まきさだラーメン（1,100円）。たっぷりのネギと細切りチャーシューがのった京都風の醤油ラーメンで、動物系の出汁の旨みをしっかり感じつつ後味はすっきり。パツッと歯切れのいいストレート細麺と、じんわり広がるスープのコク、香り高いネギが身上。セット（ごはん・焼売）は+300円で、焼売はクワイ入りのジューシーな一品。夏には冷やしラーメン（1,200円）などの季節限定も登場する。

anecdotes.text: 看板の『まきさだラーメン』は、母体の創作中華店『京中華 牧定』でまかないとして出していたネギそばを、ラーメンとして再構築した一杯。
ラーメンは『まきさだラーメン』の一種類のみという潔い構成で、ごはんと焼売のセットを付けられる。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: leafkyotoで2026/4/27開業・中京区高倉通二条西入・『京中華 牧定』が手がける・カウンター10席・まきさだラーメン1100円(牧定のまかないネギそばを再構築)・ネギと細切りチャーシューの京都風醤油・セット+300円(ごはん/焼売)・クワイ入り焼売・夏の冷やし1200円・世代を超えて愛される店をという店主の言葉を確認。shiyakusho-lunchでラーメンは一種のみ・セット・立地を確認。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: 看板のまきさだラーメンは醤油ラーメンで、醤油（しょうゆ）ベースのタレを用いる。通常のしょうゆは小麦を含むため、グルテン回避者には不向き。

vegan_cross_contact.text: スープは動物系の出汁で、トッピングは細切りチャーシュー（豚）、サイドの焼売も豚肉。植物性のみの選択肢は確認できない。

cultural_comfort.note: A small 10-seat counter ramen shop run by a long-established Kyoto Chinese restaurant; staff likely operate in Japanese, so basic Japanese or a translation app will smooth the visit.

kyr_ramen_buta_yado.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. The bowls are built on house-made wheat noodles (中太の角ストレート麺 with egg white added for a wheat aroma), seasoned with Kyoto Goko soy sauce tare, which is wheat-based. No gluten-free noodle or tare option is offered and no allergy/cross-contamination handling is described anywhere. A celiac or gluten-sensitive diner cannot safely eat the ramen here.
kyr_ramen_buta_yado.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The entire concept is pork-centric: the broth is made solely from animal ingredients (豚ウデ肉・背脂 — pork arm meat and back fat), and the shop's identity is generous chashu (sliced pork). The soy-sauce tare and side dishes are pork-based as well. There is no vegetable broth or plant-based bowl.
kyr_ramen_buta_yado.notes: [Mom & Pop] Opened February 7, 2026 in the Nishi-Kamogamo / Omiya-Yakushiyama corner of Kita-ku, taking over a space that had previously housed another ramen shop. It is a small independent counter built around one idea: a Kyoto bowl you could eat every single day.

chef_bio.background: Opened February 7, 2026 in the Nishi-Kamogamo / Omiya-Yakushiyama corner of Kita-ku, taking over a space that had previously housed another ramen shop. It is a small independent counter built around one idea: a Kyoto bowl you could eat every single day.
chef_bio.philosophy: "毎日食べられるラーメン" — ramen you can eat every day. The seasoning is kept gentle on purpose, the chashu is cooked soft so it appeals across all ages, and the noodles are made in-house: medium-thick angular straight noodles at 25% hydration, rested a day, with egg white worked in to push the wheat aroma that Kyoto diners favor.
chef_bio.specialty: The house pork-shoyu ramen. The broth is a pork clear-soup (豚清湯) made from only pork arm meat and back fat — deliberately no pork bone — so it lands light yet rich ("あっさりコクうま"), then seasoned with Goko (五光), a traditional Kyoto soy sauce, for that familiar nostalgic Kyoto sharpness. The signature move is chashu, piled without restraint: the standard Buta-yado Ramen (¥950) carries 150g, and the Buta-yado Chashu-men (¥1,200) goes to a 210g mountain of tender, thinly-sliced pork arm. A lighter Buta-yasumi Ramen (¥700) keeps just 30g for a quieter bowl.

anecdotes.text: The owner names Daiichi Asahi and Ramen Fuji — pillars of old-school Kyoto ramen — as the inspiration for the style, positioning Buta-yado as a torch-carrier for the traditional Kyoto bowl rather than a trend chaser.

The broth is described as evoking nostalgia for Kyoto residents — 'no off-smell or funk, with pork umami, richness and the sharpness of soy' — and regulars flag the chashu portions as a destination for people who simply want a lot of tender pork.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: osumitukiで2026/2/7開業・北区西加茂/大宮・『毎日食べられるラーメン』・豚清湯(腕肉と背脂のみ、豚骨不使用)・五光醤油・自家製麺(加水25%・一晩寝かせ・卵白入り)・チャーシュー量(700円30g/950円150g/1200円210g)・第一旭/ラーメンふじを手本に、を確認。kyo-sokuで立地・豚清湯の懐かしい味わい・チャーシューの多さを裏付け。店主名は非公開でnull。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Bowls are built on house-made wheat noodles and a wheat-based Kyoto soy-sauce (Goko) tare; everything passes through the same shared noodle water and kitchen, so gluten is unavoidable and cross-contact is pervasive.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The tare is built on Goko, a traditional Kyoto soy sauce — a standard fermented soy sauce that contains wheat.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The broth is made exclusively from pork (arm meat and back fat) and the shop's whole identity is heaped pork chashu; there is no plant-based option and animal product is in every bowl.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, casual neighborhood Kyoto ramen counter aimed at locals; no English is indicated, so a few words of Japanese or a pointing-at-the-menu approach will make ordering smoother.

kyr_menya_tsuki.gf_detail: This is an abura-soba and ramen shop: the noodles are wheat (made by long-established Kyoto noodle maker Menya Teigaku) and the signature dish is dressed in a house sweet-spicy soy (shoyu) tare, which is wheat-based. There is no published gluten-free menu or any allergen accommodation. Not suitable for celiac diners.
kyr_menya_tsuki.vegan_detail: The menu centers on abura-soba topped with pork chashu and stewed pork (kakuni), plus chicken-broth and dashi (fish/seafood) noodle bowls and Okayama-style fried chicken. No vegan or vegetarian option is advertised.
kyr_menya_tsuki.hours_raw: 11:00-14:30, 17:00-1:30 the next day (irregular days off, closures announced on Instagram)
kyr_menya_tsuki.notes: [Mom & Pop] 麺屋 月 is a small abura-soba specialist that opened on February 22, 2026 in Kyoto's Shimogamo neighborhood, on Kitaoji-dori near Kyoto Prefectural University in what is a competitive local ramen district. It is an intimate counter-and-table spot with just over a dozen seats.

chef_bio.background: 麺屋 月 is a small abura-soba specialist that opened on February 22, 2026 in Kyoto's Shimogamo neighborhood, on Kitaoji-dori near Kyoto Prefectural University in what is a competitive local ramen district. It is an intimate spot of about seven tables seating roughly fourteen guests.
chef_bio.philosophy: The shop leans on quality where it counts: the thick noodles come from Menya Teigaku, a venerable Kyoto noodle maker founded in 1931, and the abura-soba is built to be enjoyed first as-is, then re-seasoned partway through with chili oil and vinegar to change the flavor.
chef_bio.specialty: The signature bowl is abura-soba (brothless mixed noodles): extra-thick noodles tossed in a house-made sweet-and-spicy shoyu tare and fragrant aroma oil, finished with chashu or stewed pork belly (kakuni), menma, soft-boiled egg, shredded nori and white negi. Portions step up generously by weight, from 200g up to 500g for the same modest price band.

anecdotes.text: The extra-thick noodles are supplied by Menya Teigaku (麺屋棣鄂), a Kyoto noodle maker established in 1931, and are praised for a firm, chewy bite that holds up to the heavy tare.
Abura-soba is offered in four sizes at the same low price ladder (200g ¥850, 300g ¥900, 400g ¥950, 500g ¥1000), making it easy to size up for a bigger appetite.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: osumitukiで2026/2/22開業・左京区下鴨/北大路通(京都府立大近く)・7卓14席ほど・自家製の甘辛醤油ダレと香味油の極太麺油そば・麺は麺屋棣鄂(1931年創業)製・トッピング(チャーシュー/角煮/メンマ/味玉/海苔/白ネギ)・200g850円〜500g1000円の増量・そのまま→ラー油と酢で味変、を確認。店主名は非公開でnull。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The signature abura-soba is dressed in a house-made sweet-spicy soy (shoyu) tare, which is wheat-based; combined with the wheat noodles this dish is not gluten-free.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, recently opened neighborhood noodle counter where ordering in basic Japanese (and pointing at the menu) will be smoothest; no indication of English service.

kyr_kyo_ramen_sadakazu.gf_detail: Not gluten-free and not celiac-safe. The bowl uses thin, low-hydration straight wheat noodles in a soy-sauce (shoyu) tare that almost certainly contains wheat, plus a chicken/pork broth. There is no gluten-free menu, no dedicated equipment, and no allergy information published. This is a tiny single-owner late-night counter shop and should be treated as unsafe for anyone avoiding gluten.
kyr_kyo_ramen_sadakazu.vegan_detail: No vegan options. The signature bowl is built on a chicken-bone soy-sauce (shoyu) broth finished with pork back-fat (seabura) and chashu pork, so it is fundamentally animal-based. No vegetable or vegan ramen is offered, and no sources indicate any plant-based accommodation. A vegan diner has nothing suitable here.
kyr_kyo_ramen_sadakazu.hours_raw: 22:00-1:00 the next day (Mon-Sat); occasional irregular daytime service. Closed Sun and holidays. Open only for about three late-night hours, and often sells out at around 35 servings.
kyr_kyo_ramen_sadakazu.notes: [Mom & Pop] Sadakazu is a late-night Gion institution that earned the nickname "幻のラーメン" (phantom ramen) because it opens only for about three hours after 10 p.m. and often sells out after roughly 35 bowls. The shop relocated from the Bohana area of Fushimi Ward to the basement of the Gion Fi

chef_bio.origin: Kyoto (Gion, Higashiyama-ku); relocated from Fushimi-ku, Kyoto.
chef_bio.background: Sadakazu is a late-night Gion institution that earned the nickname "幻のラーメン" (phantom ramen) because it opens only for about three hours after 10 p.m. and often sells out after roughly 35 bowls. The shop relocated from Fushimi Ward to the basement (B1F) of the Gion First Building, a move into prime Gion territory that — along with television exposure — turned it into a sought-after late-night and post-drinking destination. It is a solo-run six-seat counter.
chef_bio.philosophy: The broth is a mellow soy flavoring with deep umami — a back-fat 'seabura chaccha' style that stays drinkable rather than heavy ('背脂ちゃっちゃ系だが、そんなに油はきつくない。まろやかな醤油ダシ'), the kind of bowl meant to cap off a night out in Gion.
chef_bio.specialty: Its signature is a Kyoto-style back-fat soy-sauce ramen (背脂醤油ラーメン, 'seabura chaccha'): a clean chicken-bone shoyu broth blanketed with pork back-fat, paired with thin, low-hydration straight noodles and chashu (¥700). A 'special' version (¥900) upgrades the chashu, and a chilled ramen appears in summer.

anecdotes.text: Open only about 22:00–01:00 and run entirely by one person from a six-seat counter, the shop typically sells out after roughly 35 bowls, which is why it is called a 'phantom' ramen that is hard to actually catch open.
It moved from Fushimi Ward into the basement of the Gion First Building, and that move plus TV appearances drove its breakout popularity as a late-night/after-drinking ramen.
The bowl became well-known enough that Ace Cook released a cup noodle 'supervised by owner 樹下真一' recreating the shop's signature 背油醤油ラーメン (released Oct 18, 2021).

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotopiで『幻のラーメン』・22時台〜25時頃の約3時間営業・一人営業・約35杯で売切・伏見区から祇園ファーストビルB1へ移転・TV出演・背脂ちゃっちゃのまろやか醤油・細麺低加水・700円/特製900円/夏は冷やし、を確認。cupmen-reviewでエースコックの監修カップ麺(2021/10/18)と店主名『樹下真一』を確認しchef_nameに追記。'坊花'の地区名は未確認のため伏見区に丸めた。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water; the dish is built on a wheat-containing soy-sauce tare. No gluten-free handling is mentioned anywhere.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The broth is a soy-sauce (shoyu) base, which in standard Japanese ramen contains wheat-fermented soy sauce; no wheat-free tare is indicated.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Broth is chicken-bone based and finished with pork back-fat and chashu pork; there is no separate vegan preparation.

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny, late-night, Japanese-only counter run solo by the owner — expect to order simply in Japanese, eat quickly, and not linger; little to no English support.

kyr_gion_kyoto_ramen.gf_detail: This is a wheat-noodle shoyu ramen shop: the noodles are wheat, the tare is soy-sauce based (Japanese shoyu typically contains wheat), and the broth uses pork and back fat. No gluten-free menu, noodle, or preparation is indicated. Not suitable for celiac diners.
